analyst_view.overall: Real Madrid are 2nd on a perfect 12 points under José Mourinho. PSV are 24th on 4 points and need results to stay in the playoff places. Madrid are close to full strength: Vinícius is back after a four-game LaLiga ban, Mbappé, Tchouaméni and Bernardo Silva shook off minor knocks from international duty, and Mendy is fit again. Rodrygo and Asencio are still long-term absentees. Mourinho has talked up squad rotation, and Madrid also host Celta on 21 November. PSV may be without Sergiño Dest, whom Bosz would not risk, and Schouten, Nagalo, Pléa and Ouaissa are out long-term; the numbers' recent form already reflects those long absences. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say a high 4.6 goals, built on Madrid's 19 goals in their last six (+1.5%). Mourinho's talk of rotation could lower it a little, but Dest's likely absence weakens PSV's defence, so the news points both ways. I stay at 4.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners and already trim both sides (-3% and -7%) for their low recent corner counts. Nothing in the team news changes the pattern, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, close to both teams' usual rates. Vinícius returns from a domestic ban for a hair-pulling incident, but it doesn't apply in Europe and his card record is already in the numbers. No referee is named, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.0 shots, including Madrid's heavy recent shooting (+5%). PSV under Bosz press high and take plenty of shots themselves, which is already in their record. I stay at 31.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.6 on target, with Madrid's sharp recent finishing counted (+7.5%). Mbappé and Vinícius both look available, and PSV's attack is unchanged by the news, so I stay at 12.6.
